Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 56
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: European
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Dancer
  trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another
  pcl5: 62

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Certain Songs: Certain songs, Crowding/Overstimulation: Crowded spaces, Crash Imagery: Cars hit by accident
  Maladaptive Strategies: Past Dwelling: I dwell on how I used to be before the event, Avoid Location: Going to or near the place where the event happened, Suppress Thoughts: try hard not think about the trauma
  Threat: Concentration: Having difficulty concentrating, Cannot Relax: I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place, Sleep Vigilance: I have difficulty falling asleep because I need to stay alert
  Negative Appraisals: Inaction Guilt: I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened, Failed to Protect: I should have protected others and I failed, Failed Role: I have failed in my most important role in life

Vignette:
Marco's feet used to move with a fluidity that belied his 56 years. As a professional dancer, he had spent decades mastering the nuances of movement, his body an instrument honed by years of practice and performance. But it was on one fateful night, after a particularly grueling rehearsal, that Marco's world began to unravel. While driving home, lost in thought, he failed to notice a pedestrian stepping into the crosswalk. The sound of crunching metal and shattering glass is forever etched in his mind. In the months following the accident, Marco became increasingly withdrawn. Certain songs that used to fill him with joy now sent him spiraling into despair – the lyrics echoing the what-ifs that plagued his every waking moment. He began to avoid crowded spaces, the cacophony of sounds and the crush of bodies overwhelming him. The sight of cars damaged in accidents would send a shiver down his spine, transporting him back to that fateful night. As Marco struggled to come to terms with what had happened, he found himself dwelling on the past – reminiscing about the carefree days when dance was his sole focus. He became fixated on how things used to be before the accident, as if clinging to memories of a bygone era could somehow undo the damage done. The thought of returning to the place where the accident occurred filled him with dread; he would go to great lengths to avoid it, taking circuitous routes and adjusting his schedule to steer clear of the area. But even in the safety of his own home, Marco couldn't shake off the feeling of unease that had taken up residence inside him. He tried hard not to think about the trauma, pushing thoughts of the accident deep down into the recesses of his mind – only for them to resurface with a vengeance when he least expected it. His concentration began to suffer; simple tasks became Herculean challenges as his mind wandered back to that night. Relaxation was a distant memory; even in the stillness of the night, Marco's body remained on high alert, waiting for the other shoe to drop. Sleep eluded him, too, as he lay awake, replaying the events leading up to the accident and wondering what he could have done differently. The weight of his perceived failures bore down on him – I should have protected that person; I failed in my most important role as a responsible driver. Marco's guilt threatened to consume him whole, as if self-recrimination was the only way to atone for his sins. The man who once moved with such fluidity now felt like he was trapped in quicksand, unable to escape the quagmire of his own negative appraisals. His relationships began to suffer; his wife, sensing his withdrawal, tried to reach out, but Marco pushed her away, convinced that he didn't deserve comfort or solace. The thought of returning to dance – an activity that once brought him so much joy – filled him with anxiety. It was only when Marco's doctor expressed concern about his escalating symptoms and the toll they were taking on his physical health that he realized he couldn't continue down this path alone. Seeking help felt like a monumental task, one that required him to confront the very demons he'd been trying so hard to suppress. But as he sat in the therapist's office, the weight of his secrets slowly beginning to lift, Marco knew that he had no choice but to face the darkness head-on – and hope that somehow, someway, he could learn to forgive himself and rediscover the beauty of movement that once brought him so much joy.
